title: Canary Deployment Controller with Automated Rollback
problem: Deploying software updates to production instances without gradual traffic shifting risks catastrophic outages when defect-laden releases escape staging environments. Progressive delivery mitigates deployment blast radiuses by routing a small fraction of real user requests to canary replicas while monitoring reliability metrics. This project implements a custom Kubernetes operator in Go that reconciles declarative CanaryDeployment resources, coordinates traffic shifting across service meshes, evaluates Prometheus service-level indicators, and triggers automated rollbacks when error rate or latency thresholds are breached.
use_cases: Progressive release management for microservices with automated error rate rollback gates
Canary latency regression detection during cloud service upgrades
Automated traffic migration across Blue-Green and canary service endpoints
hard_parts: Managing Kubernetes reconciliation loops with exponential backoff and idempotency without state desynchronization
Translating dynamic traffic weight distributions across service mesh routing objects without connection drops
Querying Prometheus metrics reliably across sliding inspection windows while handling sparse or delayed samples
Enforcing safe automated rollback state transitions during active deployments without human intervention
screener_signals: Custom Resource Definition and Go operator built using client-go and controller-runtime
Automated progressive traffic shifting verified across 4 distinct step percentages
End-to-end chaos integration test demonstrating automated rollback within 30 seconds of an injected fault

components.name: Canary Controller
components.purpose: Reconciles CanaryDeployment CRDs, tracking rollout phases and updating target pod replica counts

components.name: Traffic Routing Manager
components.purpose: Updates traffic split weights between primary and canary services via service mesh virtual routers

components.name: Metric Analyzer
components.purpose: Queries Prometheus HTTP API to compute error rates and p99 latency against configured SLO thresholds

components.name: Automated Rollback Engine
components.purpose: Shifts traffic weights back to primary version and scales canary to zero upon threshold violation

components.name: Cluster Manifest Package
components.purpose: Packages operator container and manifests for local execution on Minikube or Kind clusters

architecture.data_flow: Developers apply a CanaryDeployment manifest; the controller detects the spec change and creates a canary deployment; traffic shifts incrementally (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) across scheduled intervals; the Metric Analyzer queries Prometheus every 15 seconds; if error rates remain below threshold, rollout advances; if SLOs are violated, the Rollback Engine immediately shifts 100% traffic to stable pods and marks status FAILED.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Reconciliation loop terminates canary rollout and restores stable routing weights if error rate exceeds 5% or p99 latency exceeds 200ms.

targets.method: Measurement of request routing distribution across primary and canary pods at each progression step
targets.input: 1,000 synthetic HTTP requests routed through proxy at 10%, 25%, and 50% target weights
targets.environment: Local Kubernetes cluster (Kind/Minikube), single node, 4-core CPU
targets.minimum_pass: Observed traffic percentage within 4.0% of target weight at each progression stage
targets.target: Observed traffic percentage within 1.5% of target weight at each progression stage
targets.report: Traffic distribution summary log table from curl benchmarking client

targets.method: Injection of 10% HTTP 500 error rate into canary pods during 50% traffic stage
targets.input: Continuous background load of 100 requests per second across active pods
targets.environment: Local Kubernetes cluster (Kind/Minikube) with local Prometheus instance
targets.minimum_pass: Detection of breach and full traffic restoration to stable version in < 45 seconds
targets.target: Detection of breach and full traffic restoration to stable version in < 25 seconds
targets.report: Controller event log and Prometheus metric series showing rollback timeline

targets.method: Continuous resource monitoring of operator pod during repeated deployment reconciliations
targets.input: 5 concurrent CanaryDeployment objects under continuous metric evaluation
targets.report: kubectl top pod output log and Prometheus container memory metric

worksheet.q1: The student builds a Kubernetes operator in Go that reconciles custom CanaryDeployment resources, progressively shifts traffic via service routers, queries Prometheus metrics, and rolls back on SLO breach.
worksheet.q2: Core path: CRD definition, client-go operator, traffic routing manager, Prometheus analyzer, automated rollback, and Helm chart (29h). Extended path: Slack webhook alerts and multi-cluster traffic shifting (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: CRD & Operator (5h), Routing Integration (4h), Metric Analyzer (4h), Rollback Engine (4h), Chaos Test & Helm (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: CI/CD/DevOps/security pipelines, IaC/cloud. Metrics: Traffic Shift Progression Accuracy, Automated Rollback Duration, Controller Memory Footprint. Rejected: storage disk compression (not an OLAP project).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: client-go reconciliation idempotency, traffic weight synchronicity, Prometheus scrape window lag, and fail-safe rollback state transitions.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: mock microservice image in Go with /version, /healthz, and /inject-fault endpoints. 2 versions. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: controller-runtime envtest mode without full Kubernetes cluster.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Prometheus scrape lag delaying rollback. Fallback: configure 5s local scrape interval.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded mock logs. Anti-fake check 5 accepts dynamic error threshold at runtime and asserts live operator controller event log mutation.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local Kind/Minikube cluster only.
